label: Moved to Uppsala
description: Siegbahn continued his instrument work in Uppsala after starting in Stockholm.

sources.quote: He started building the instrument in Stockholm and continued the work in Upsala where he moved in 1954.

label: Published first accurate XPS spectrum
description: First X-ray photoelectron spectrum providing accurate atomic binding energies published with Nordling and Sokolowski.

sources.quote: The first X-ray photoelectron spectrum that could provide accurate atomic binding energies was published in 1957 ( Nordling et al., 1957 ) using an X-ray tube rather than a radioactive source.

label: Reported first chemical shift
description: First report of a chemical shift between metallic copper and CuO made by Siegbahn and colleagues.

sources.quote: In 1958 (Sokolowski et al., 1958) the first report of a chemical shift was made by Siegbahn and colleagues reporting a shift between metallic copper and CuO.

label: Sabbatical at Berkeley
description: Siegbahn spent a sabbatical year in Shirley's laboratory.

sources.quote: Siegbahn (who spent a sabbatical year in 1961 in Shirley's laboratory)

label: Published ESCA book on solids
description: Major impact book focused on solids published.

sources.quote: the 1967 book ( Siegbahn et al., 1967 ) focused on solids and the 1969 book ( Siegbahn et al., 1969) concerned with gas phase ESCA.

label: Published ESCA book on gases
description: Major impact book concerned with gas phase ESCA published.

sources.quote: the 1967 book ( Siegbahn et al., 1967 ) focused on solids and the 1969 book ( Siegbahn et al., 1969) concerned with gas phase ESCA.

label: Received Nobel Prize in Physics
description: Siegbahn received the Nobel Prize in Physics.

sources.quote: Kai Siegbahn, who received the 1981 Nobel Prize in Physics, refers to Robinson's work and his spectrum ( Figure 1) in his Nobel Prize lecture ( Siegbahn, 1981 ).

label: Delivered Nobel Lecture
description: Siegbahn gave his Nobel Prize lecture.

sources.quote: Kai Siegbahn, who received the 1981 Nobel Prize in Physics, refers to Robinson's work and his spectrum ( Figure 1) in his Nobel Prize lecture ( Siegbahn, 1981 ).

label: Interviewed by David Briggs
description: Siegbahn participated in an interview with David Briggs.

sources.quote: a delightful interview of Siegbahn by David Briggs, ( Briggs, 1982 )
